title: SQL Injection in healthcare provider authentication
description:
The authenticate_user function in src/auth/login.py constructs SQL queries by directly concatenating user input into the query string. An attacker could bypass authentication or execute arbitrary SQL commands.

**CVSS 3.1 Score: 9.8 (Critical)**
**NIST CSF**: PR.AC-1, PR.AC-2

**Remediation Priority**: Immediate - This vulnerability allows complete authentication bypass and access to all patient records.
hipaa_impact: Critical - Would allow unauthorized access to PHI
compliance_impact: Potential HIPAA violation, could trigger audit

title: Hardcoded JWT signing key in production codebase
description:
The JWT_SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in src/auth/tokens.py. If this key is compromised, an attacker can forge JWT tokens and impersonate any user in the system, including administrators.

**CVSS 3.1 Score: 9.1 (Critical)**
**NIST CSF**: PR.AC-1, PR.AT-1

**Impact**: All JWT-based authentication across the entire platform.

title: Path traversal in patient document retrieval API
description:
The download_patient_document endpoint does not validate the document_path parameter. Attackers can use '../' sequences to access files outside patient record directories, including system files and other patients' data.

**CVSS 3.1 Score: 8.1 (High)**
**NIST CSF**: PR.AC-3, PR.DS-1

**Known Exploitable**: Yes - This pattern has been exploited in similar healthcare platforms.
hipaa_impact: High - Would expose PHI from other patient records
compliance_impact: HIPAA breach notification requirement if exploited

title: NoSQL injection in clinical patient search
description:
The _build_advanced_query method in src/patients/search.py uses MongoDB query operators without input sanitization. An attacker can inject operators like $where, $ne, $regex to bypass access controls or extract data for all patients.

**CVSS 3.1 Score: 8.2 (High)**
**NIST CSF**: PR.AC-3, PR.DS-1

**Remediation Priority**: High - Active directory enumeration possible.

title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in external patient data export
description:
The export_to_external_service function accepts user-controlled URLs without validation. An attacker can target internal services, cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254), or exfiltrate patient data to attacker-controlled servers.

**CVSS 3.1 Score: 9.1 (Critical)**
**NIST CSF**: PR.PT-3, PR.DS-2

**OWASP Category**: A10:2021 - Server-Side Request Forgery
hipaa_impact: Critical - PHI could be exfiltrated to external servers

title: Missing HMAC signature verification on clinical webhooks
description:
The webhook endpoints accept any POST request without verifying HMAC signatures. Attackers can inject fabricated lab results, prescription statuses, or insurance decisions into patient records.

**CVSS 3.1 Score: 9.0 (Critical)**
**NIST CSF**: PR.AC-6, PR.DS-2

**Note**: This is a critical data integrity vulnerability for clinical decision-making.
compliance_impact: Data integrity violation affects clinical decisions

title: XML External Entity (XXE) injection in CDA clinical document parsing
description:
The process_cda_document function uses Python's default XML parser with external entity resolution enabled. Attackers can read server files, perform SSRF attacks, or cause denial of service.

**CVSS 3.1 Score: 9.1 (Critical)**
**NIST CSF**: PR.DS-1, PR.PT-3

**CWE Top 25**: Yes - Ranked #6 in 2023
hipaa_impact: Critical - PHI exposure, arbitrary file read
compliance_impact: Direct technical vulnerability in PHI processing

title: Cryptographically weak password hashing for provider accounts
description:
The PasswordHasher class uses MD5 for password hashing. MD5 is cryptographically broken and provides no protection against rainbow table attacks. Additionally, passwords are not salted.

**CVSS 3.1 Score: 9.8 (Critical)**
**NIST CSF**: PR.AC-1

**Industry Standard**: bcrypt, Argon2, or scrypt with proper work factors.
hipaa_impact: Critical - If DB compromised, all passwords immediately cracked

title: Debug mode enabled in production environment
description:
The Flask application configuration enables debug mode in production. This exposes detailed error messages with stack traces, internal implementation details, and potentially enables remote code execution through the interactive debugger.

**CVSS 3.1 Score: 7.5 (High)**
**NIST CSF**: PR.PT-2

**Note**: This was found during configuration audit, not automated scanning.
cwe_name: Entity Depends on Missing, Unavailable, or Disallowed
hipaa_impact: Medium - Information disclosure aids further attacks
compliance_impact: CISO flagged as immediate fix required

title: Multiple hardcoded secrets in application configuration
description:
The src/config.py file contains multiple hardcoded secrets: Flask SECRET_KEY, database password, and JWT secret. These fall back to known insecure defaults when environment variables are not set.

**CVSS 3.1 Score: 7.5 (High)**
**NIST CSF**: PR.AC-1, PR.DS-2

**Secrets Found**:
- Flask session secret (line 68)
- Database password (line 82)
- JWT signing key (line 91)
hipaa_impact: High - Secrets in source control = immediate rotation required
compliance_impact: AWS CloudGuard and SOX compliance flag
